Dr. '''Kim Sunghoon''' is a South Korean [[biologist]].

==Education==
*1981   B.S. [[Seoul National University]]
*1983   M.S. [[Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology]]
*1991   Ph.D. [[Brown University]], U.S.

==Work==
Sunghoon Kim has been studying novel functions of human [[aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases]] (ARSs) and searching for their pathophysiological connections to human diseases (PNAS 105:11043,<ref>[http://www.pnas.org/content/105/32/11043.long Aminoacyl tRNA synthetases and their connections to disease<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> 2008; Nat Rev Cancer 11:708, 2011<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://www.nature.com/nrc/journal/v11/n10/full/nrc3124.html|doi = 10.1038/nrc3124|title = Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases and tumorigenesis: More than housekeeping|year = 2011|last1 = Kim|first1 = Sunghoon|last2 = You|first2 = Sungyong|last3 = Hwang|first3 = Daehee|journal = Nature Reviews Cancer|volume = 11|issue = 10|pages = 708–718|pmid = 21941282|s2cid = 44712015|url-access = subscription}}</ref>). He has identified potent novel tumor suppressors such as AIMP2/p38 (Nat Genet 34:330, 2003<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://www.nature.com/ng/journal/v34/n3/full/ng1182.html|doi = 10.1038/ng1182|title = Downregulation of FUSE-binding protein and c-myc by tRNA synthetase cofactor p38 is required for lung cell differentiation|year = 2003|last1 = Kim|first1 = Min Jung|last2 = Park|first2 = Bum-Joon|last3 = Kang|first3 = Young-Sun|last4 = Kim|first4 = Hyoung June|last5 = Park|first5 = Jae-Hyun|last6 = Kang|first6 = Jung Woo|last7 = Lee|first7 = Sang Won|last8 = Han|first8 = Jung Min|last9 = Lee|first9 = Han-Woong|last10 = Kim|first10 = Sunghoon|journal = Nature Genetics|volume = 34|issue = 3|pages = 330–336|pmid = 12819782|s2cid = 41006480|url-access = subscription}}</ref>), AIMP3/p18 (Cell, 120:209, 2005<ref>[http://www.cell.com/abstract/S0092-8674(05)00002-4 Cell - The Haploinsufficient Tumor Suppressor p18 Upregulates p53 via Interactions with ATM/ATR<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>). Besides, he has also investigated novel extracellular activities of ARSs and associated factors such as lysyl-tRNA synthetase (KRS) (PNAS 102, 6356, 2005<ref>[http://www.pnas.org/content/102/18/6356.long Human lysyl-tRNA synthetase is secreted to trigger proinflammatory response<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>), tryptophanyl-tRNA synthetase(WRS)(Nat Struct Mol Biol 11:149, 2004<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://www.nature.com/nsmb/journal/v11/n2/full/nsmb722.html|doi = 10.1038/nsmb722|title = A short peptide insertion crucial for angiostatic activity of human tryptophanyl-tRNA synthetase|year = 2004|last1 = Kise|first1 = Yoshiaki|last2 = Lee|first2 = Sang Won|last3 = Park|first3 = Sang Gyu|last4 = Fukai|first4 = Shuya|last5 = Sengoku|first5 = Toru|last6 = Ishii|first6 = Ryohei|last7 = Yokoyama|first7 = Shigeyuki|last8 = Kim|first8 = Sunghoon|last9 = Nureki|first9 = Osamu|journal = Nature Structural & Molecular Biology|volume = 11|issue = 2|pages = 149–156|pmid = 14730354|s2cid = 20084521|url-access = subscription}}</ref>) and AIMP1/p43 (PNAS 103:14913, 2006<ref>[http://www.pnas.org/content/103/40/14913.long Hormonal activity of AIMP1/p43 for glucose homeostasis<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>). He also discovered the oncogenic variant of AIMP2, designated AIMP2-DX2, as one of the critical factors that determines the survival of lung cancer patients (Plos Genet 7:e1001351, 2011<ref>[http://www.plosgenetics.org/article/info%3Adoi%2F10.1371%2Fjournal.pgen.1001351 PLOS Genetics: Cancer-Associated Splicing Variant of Tumor Suppressor AIMP2/p38: Pathological Implication in Tumorigenesis<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>). More recently{{when|date=March 2024}}, he found that leucyl-tRNA synthetase (LRS) serves as an amino acid sensor for mTOR signal pathway (Cell 149:410, 2012<ref>[http://www.cell.com/abstract/S0092-8674(12)00282-6 Cell - Leucyl-tRNA Synthetase Is an Intracellular Leucine Sensor for the mTORC1-Signaling Pathway<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>).

*1991 – 1994: Post-doc, [[MIT]] 
*1994 – 2001: Associate Professor, [[Sung Kyun Kwan University]]
*2001 – present: Professor, [[Seoul National University]]
*1988 – 2007: Director, Center for ARS Network National Creative Research Initiatives 
*2007 – 2010: Director, Center for Medicinal Protein Network and Systems Biology
*2010 – present: Director, Medicinal Bioconvergence Research Center
